# Case selection, controls and verification

*This file is generated by `scripts/render_docs.py` from `data/cases/cases.csv`, `data/cases/excluded.csv` and the
verified build outputs. Do not edit by hand.*

## Two cohorts

* **Development cohort** - cases I picked from memory of famous US accounting failures of the XBRL era (2009 onward) and looked up on EDGAR. This is a hindsight list, not a sample;
  the models were built while looking at these cases.
* **Holdout cohort** - cases found *mechanically* from SEC's public Accounting and Auditing Enforcement Release (AAER) list, under rules committed to GitHub (`docs/preregistration.md`, commit `f0f6cb5`)
  before any of them was scored. Every candidate that passed was kept; the 32 that did not pass are listed at the end with the reason.

## How cases were found and kept

1. **Candidates.** Development: from memory. Holdout: every company respondent in an AAER dated 2012-01-01 or later whose name resolves to an EDGAR registrant that is non-financial and filed an Item 4.02 8-K between mid-2010 and the AAER date.
2. **Primary source.** A case is kept only if EDGAR holds an **8-K with Item 4.02** (non-reliance on previously issued financial statements).
   `make data` re-checks that the cited accession exists, carries Item 4.02 and was filed on the stated date, and aborts otherwise.
3. **Usable before the event.** At least one *original* 10-K filed **before** the cut-off, with XBRL data, must cover a fiscal year that the 8-K (and, for the holdout, the SEC order as well) names as misstated.
   Those years (and only those) are labelled positive.
4. **Corroboration.** An SEC enforcement release concerning the same matter (URL and date below); a Chapter 11 8-K (Item 1.03) is looked up on EDGAR for each case and shown where it exists.
5. **Date the problem became public.** The Item 4.02 filing date. Where I could read an earlier company filing that disclosed the issue (NT 10-K/10-Q, 8-K), that earlier date becomes the look-ahead cut-off instead.
   No filing on or after the cut-off is ever scored.
6. **Same matter.** For the holdout I read the 4.02 text against the AAER title and excluded a pair only if it was clearly a different matter; none needed excluding.
7. **Anything unverifiable is dropped, not guessed** (lists at the end).

## Controls (80 healthy peers)

For each case, three controls were chosen by this deterministic rule (`src/redflag/controls.py`):

* US-located company filing 10-Ks with XBRL data (XBRL `frames` API, `loc` starts with `US`);
* not a financial company (SIC 6000-6799);
* total assets within a factor of 4 of the case at its first misstated fiscal year, **nearest first**;
* industry tier: same 3-digit SIC first, then same 2-digit SIC, then same SIC division (the tier is recorded; result: 39 at 3-digit SIC, 28 at 2-digit SIC, 13 at SIC division);
* **no Item 4.02 8-K anywhere in the company's EDGAR history**;
* a usable 10-K (all required Beneish inputs) for every fiscal year the matched case is labelled misstated, so cases and controls are
  compared in **the same fiscal years**;
* each control is used for one case only.

### Selection-bias acknowledgement

* Cases are chosen with hindsight from famous failures that also had XBRL data. Detectors look better on such cases than on the unknown cases
  a prospective screen has to find.
* Companies whose misstatement pre-dates their XBRL data (e.g. much of 2009-2011 for smaller filers) are systematically excluded.
* "Healthy" means only "no Item 4.02 filing on EDGAR". It does not rule out undisclosed restatements ("stealth" corrections in later
  filings), SEC investigations, or enforcement actions without a restatement. Contamination of the control group would bias results
  *against* the detector; I have no way of measuring its size.
* Matching on size and industry removes the grossest confounders, but not growth, leverage, M&A activity or accounting-policy
  differences, all of which move the Beneish ratios.
* Three controls per case were fixed in advance by the author, not tuned. Any case with fewer than three eligible peers is listed in the build log below.
